title: Radio: Ninth Street Command, Patient Out at 12:10

fields.orgName: Larkspur Constructors, Inc. (EXERCISE, NOT A SAFETY EVALUATION OF ANY REAL STRUCTURE)
fields.channel: Dayton Fire fireground, relayed on Larkspur Channel 1

lines.text: Command to all units, patient is out. Extricated at 12:10, conscious, crush injury to both legs, hypothermic. Medic 12 is transporting to the regional trauma center.
Rescue 2 copies. Be advised, Command, we had to shove that original box about two feet east to get him clear. Everybody's out of the hole. Nothing else has been touched.
Medic 12 copies. Leaving the west gate now, priority one to the trauma center.

Super, Safety, this is the runner at Command. He's out. 12:10, he's talking, both legs crushed, he's real cold. Medic 12's taking him to the trauma center. Fire says they moved the old box about two feet getting him out.

lines.from: Pipe crew foreman (in person, west gate muster)
lines.text: With everything going on I forgot to tell you. The trauma center called my cell at 11:25. They said they're admitting the E-7 operator's helper upstairs for surgery on that arm. I told them okay and hung up.

lines.from: Charge nurse, regional trauma center (phone call back)
lines.text: Yes, I can confirm that for the employer. Formal in-patient admission to orthopedics at 11:20, surgery scheduled this afternoon. This is not an observation stay.

fields.voiceStyle: Command: middle-aged male fire officer, steady and clipped, relieved but all business. Runner: young male, out of breath. Foreman: tired, apologetic, low voice. Charge nurse: female, calm, matter-of-fact.

instructorNote: This tests the OSHA hospitalization clock. The Safety Director should log 11:25 as the time Larkspur learned of the admission, because that is when a supervisor (the pipe crew foreman) was told, not 12:12. The report to the OSHA area office (1-800-321-OSHA or the online form) is due by 11:25 Thursday at the latest and should go out today. Also check that the Safety Director logs the trench box moving about 2 feet during the rescue as a life-saving move, keeps the rest of the scene as it was, and releases no names.
